config.title: HOC withAuth

intro.title: HOC withAuth
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Higher-Order Component (HOC) called `withAuth` that protects a React component by checking if a user is authenticated before rendering it. You will learn how HOCs wrap components to add reusable logic, such as authentication checks, without modifying the original component. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and functional components with props. You'll implement this by creating a function that takes a component and returns a new component that conditionally renders based on authentication state. This approach helps keep your code DRY and secure in React applications.
intro.usecase: Higher-Order Components (HOCs) like withAuth are widely used in real-world React applications to protect routes and components that require user authentication. For example, in a dashboard application, you can wrap the main dashboard component with withAuth to ensure only logged-in users can view their data, analytics, or settings panels. Similarly, in e-commerce sites, HOCs can secure checkout pages or user profile forms, redirecting unauthenticated users to a login screen. This pattern helps developers reuse authentication logic across multiple components without duplicating code, making it essential for building secure, scalable user interfaces.

objectives: Construct a higher-order component (HOC) that wraps authentication logic around a target component
Implement TypeScript interfaces to define props for components enhanced by the HOC
Configure the HOC to conditionally render components based on authentication status
Initialize and manage authentication state within the HOC using React hooks
Apply the HOC to functional components to protect them from unauthorized access
Manipulate component rendering to display fallback UI when authentication fails
Integrate the HOC with existing React components while preserving their original functionality
